statements.claim: Narada, having heard reports of Dwaraka, came to see Krishna's city and household for himself, walking among the palaces of Krishna's sixteen thousand queens and finding Krishna present and fully engaged in every palace.
statements.evidence: Corpus chain: previous story DKS_0284 (SB 10.69.1-35, evt_0257) — 'Narada Sees Krishna in Every Palace of Dvaraka... simultaneously present in each of the 16,000 palaces performing different duties.'

statements.claim: Narada declared he now understood Krishna's yoga-maya, which even the masters of illusion cannot see, revealed to him through serving Krishna's feet.
statements.evidence: SB 10.69.37 'vidāma yoga-māyās te durdarśā api māyinām'; pack excerpt: 'I understand your yoga-maya, hard to see even for the master of maya, revealed to me by serving your feet'.

statements.claim: Krishna was following the path of men in Dwaraka — living a mortal king's life — while carrying the power that upholds all worlds.
statements.evidence: SB 10.69.43 'evaṁ manuṣya-padavīm anuvartamāno nārāyaṇo 'khila-bhavāya gṛhīta-śaktiḥ' (Narayana following the path of men, having assumed power for the good of all).

statements.claim: Krishna bade Narada wander the worlds singing of his pastimes, and the telling of them purifies whoever hears.
statements.evidence: Pack excerpt: 'Krishna bade him roam the worlds singing his purifying pastimes'; SB 10.69.38 (Narada seeks leave to flood the worlds with Krishna's glory); 10.69.44 'yo gāyati śṛṇoty anumodate... bhaktir bhaved bhagavati hy apavarga-mārge'.

statements.claim: Narada departed and went singing through the worlds, and those who sing of, hear of, or delight in these deeds turn toward the path of liberation.
statements.evidence: Pack excerpt: 'Narada departed remembering him'; SB 10.69.44 ties singing/hearing/delighting to devotion on the path of liberation (apavarga-mārga).

statements.claim: The scenes of Krishna at ease with ministers, listening to singers, beside queens at lamps, and laughing with children are the ordinary texture of his Dwaraka days.
statements.evidence: Atmospheric elaboration of Krishna's simultaneous presence in each palace (corpus chain DKS_0284); generic domestic vignettes, no independent factual assertion.

notes: All event claims (yoga-maya declaration, command to roam and sing, departure) directly supported by SB 10.69.36-44 excerpt and verses; multi-palace simultaneity carried by corpus chain DKS_0284.

statements.claim: The birds of Dwaraka sang at dawn like bards awakening Krishna.
statements.evidence: SB 10.70.1 'vayāṁsy aroruvan kṛṣṇaṁ bodhayantīva vandinaḥ' (the birds cried out, awakening Krishna as it were, like bards).

statements.claim: In the brahma-muhurta, Rukmini lay awake beside Krishna and could not bear the coming moment (the end of their night together).
statements.evidence: SB 10.70.2 'muhūrtaṁ taṁ tu vaidarbhī nāmṛṣyad ati-śobhanam' (Vaidarbhi/Rukmini could not endure that most beautiful moment); 10.70.3 'brāhme muhūrta utthāya vāry upaspṛśya mādhavaḥ'.

statements.claim: Krishna rose in the brahma-muhurta, touched water, and meditated on the one self-effulgent reality that is secondless, immutable, and free of all impurity.
statements.evidence: SB 10.70.3-4 'ekaṁ svayaṁ-jyotir ananyam avyayaṁ... nitya-nirasta-kalmaṣam'.

statements.claim: He bathed in clear water according to rite, put on fresh garments, performed the sandhya worship and fed the sacred fire while keeping his speech still.
statements.evidence: SB 10.70.5 'athāpluto 'mbhasy amale yathā-vidhi... cakāra sandhyopagamādi... hutānalo brahma jajāpa vāg-yataḥ'.

statements.claim: He saluted the rising sun and offered the first worship of the day to his own senses.
statements.evidence: SB 10.70.6 'upasthāyārkam udyantaṁ tarpayitvātmanaḥ kalāḥ' (worshiped the rising sun, gratifying his own senses). The story's gloss ('asking them to serve him rather than rule him') is interpretive.

statements.claim: Every day Krishna gave away herds of milk-giving cows with horns of gold, hooves of silver, strung with pearls, together with linen and sesame.
statements.evidence: SB 10.70.7-8 'dhenūnāṁ rukma-śṛṅgīnāṁ sādhvīnāṁ mauktika-srajām... dadau rūpya-khurāgrāṇāṁ kṣaumājina-tilaiḥ saha'.

statements.claim: He honored the cows, brahmanas, gods, elders, teachers, and every living being, then adorned himself, ornament of the human world.
statements.evidence: SB 10.70.9-10 'go-vipra-devatā-vṛddha-gurūn bhūtāni sarvaśaḥ... ātmānaṁ bhūṣayām āsa nara-loka-vibhūṣaṇam'.

statements.claim: He looked into the mirror at the auspicious objects — clarified butter, cows and bulls, brahmanas, images of the gods — and gave garlands, betel leaf and unguents to the brahmanas.
statements.evidence: SB 10.70.11-12 'avekṣyājyaṁ tathādarśaṁ go-vṛṣa-dvija-devatāḥ... saṁvibhajyāgrato viprān srak-tāmbūlānulepanaiḥ'.

statements.claim: His charioteer brought the great chariot; Krishna took the driver's hand and mounted, watched by the women of the inner palace with shy, loving glances.
statements.evidence: SB 10.70.13-15 'sūta upānīya syandanaṁ... gṛhītvā pāṇinā pāṇī sārathes tam athāruhat'; 'īkṣito 'ntaḥ-pura-strīṇāṁ sa-vrīḍa-prema-vīkṣitaiḥ'.

statements.claim: He rode to the Sudharma assembly hall of the Yadus, surrounded by the Vrishnis (including Uddhava and Satyaki), took the highest seat illuminating the quarters, and was entertained by jesting ministers and music of mridanga, vina, flute, cymbals and conch.
statements.evidence: SB 10.70.16-19 'sudharmākhyāṁ sabhāṁ sarvair vṛṣṇibhiḥ parivāritaḥ... paramāsane vibhur babhau sva-bhāsā kakubho 'vabhāsayan... nānā-hāsya-rasair... mṛdaṅga-vīṇā-muraja-veṇu-tāla-dara-svanaiḥ'; Uddhava and Satyaki named in pack index characters.

statements.claim: Closing reflection — Krishna performed the rites as a servant of the Lord within, and his service meant serving everyone who came before him — is devotional commentary rather than event.
statements.evidence: Pack offers no such statement; it is interpretive framing consistent with the worship sequence.

notes: Every narrated action maps 1:1 to SB 10.70.1-19; no unsupported or contradicted factual claims.

statements.claim: Sudama was a learned, self-controlled brahmana living in a poor village in great poverty.
statements.evidence: Pack excerpt: 'Sudama, a learned and self-controlled brahmana living in great poverty'; SB 10.80.6 'yadṛcchayopapannena vartamāno gṛhāśramī'.

statements.claim: His devoted wife urged him to visit Krishna, his boyhood friend who now dwelt in Dwaraka as lord of the Bhoja, Vrishni and Andhaka peoples, saying Krishna would give them wealth.
statements.evidence: SB 10.80.7-10: wife speaks with a wan face; 'sākṣāc chriyaḥ patiḥ... āste 'dhunā dvāravatyāṁ bhoja-vṛṣṇy-andhakeśvaraḥ'; pack excerpt confirms she says Krishna will give them wealth.

statements.claim: The wife asked again and again, and at last Sudama resolved in his mind to go.
statements.evidence: SB 10.80.11-12 'sa evaṁ bhāryayā vipro bahuśaḥ prārthito muhuḥ / iti sañcintya manasā gamanāya matiṁ dadhe'.

statements.claim: Sudama begged four handfuls of flattened rice from the brahmanas of the village, tied them in a rag, and set out for Dwaraka.
statements.evidence: SB 10.80.13-14 'yācitvā caturo muṣṭīn viprān pṛthuka-taṇḍulān / sa tān ādāya viprāgryaḥ prayayau dvārakāṁ kila' (he, best of brahmanas, having begged four fistfuls of flat rice from the brahmanas, took them and went to Dvaraka). Story follows the passage reading (Sudama begs); pack excerpt phrasing 'she borrows' reflects a common retelling but the Sanskrit passage is authoritative here and supports the story.

statements.claim: Walking the long road, he wondered how he would ever gain sight of Krishna, the lord of a great city.
statements.evidence: Pack excerpt: Sudama 'sets out for Dwaraka wondering how he may gain sight of Krishna'; SB 10.80.15-16.

statements.claim: He crossed the outer groves and the three gates/enclosures and reached the palace of the king who had sixteen thousand queens.
statements.evidence: SB 10.80.15-16 'trīṇi gulmāny atīyāya tisraḥ kakṣāś ca sa-dvijaḥ / gṛhaṁ dvy-aṣṭa-sahasrāṇāṁ mahiṣīṇāṁ harer' (passed three camps and three enclosures, the house of Hari with sixteen thousand queens).

statements.claim: Krishna had once been a boy at the guru's house with Sudama.
statements.evidence: Boyhood friendship stated in pack excerpt ('his boyhood friend'); guru-kula shared past confirmed by SB 10.80.26 (next story's verses: 'gāthāḥ pūrvā guru-kule satoḥ') via corpus chain.

statements.claim: Sudama's remembered image of Krishna as a hungry, ragged boy like himself is sentimental coloring.
statements.evidence: No pack statement that Krishna was poor as a boy; emotional parallel, not a sourceable fact.

notes: All core events (poverty, wife's urging, resolve, four fistfuls of flat rice, journey, wonder at gaining sight) supported by SB 10.80.5-16.

statements.claim: Sudama stood before the palace housing Krishna's sixteen thousand queens.
statements.evidence: SB 10.80.16 (from previous pack's final verse, continued here): 'gṛhaṁ dvy-aṣṭa-sahasrāṇāṁ mahiṣīṇāṁ harer'; palace setting per pack index.

statements.claim: Seeing Sudama from afar, Krishna rose from the couch where he sat with Rukmini, ran to him and embraced his old friend with tears of joy.
statements.evidence: SB 10.80.17-18 'taṁ vilokyācyuto dūrāt priyā-paryaṅkam āsthitaḥ... aṅga-saṅgāti-nirvṛtaḥ'; pack excerpt: 'rises from Rukmini's couch, runs to him, and embraces his old friend with tears of joy'.

statements.claim: Krishna seated Sudama on his own couch, washed his feet, and bore the water on his own head.
statements.evidence: SB 10.80.19-20 'athopaveśya paryaṅke svayam sakhyuḥ samarhaṇam / agrahīc chirasā... bhagavāṁl loka-pāvanaḥ'.

statements.claim: He had fragrant incense brought and rows of lamps lit, and received his friend with joy.
statements.evidence: SB 10.80.21 'dhūpaiḥ surabhibhir mitraṁ pradīpāvalibhir mudā'.

statements.claim: The women of the palace, seeing a destitute beggar in a torn cloth honored by Krishna, whispered what merit this man had done that the guru of the three worlds and the abode of Shri should cherish him.
statements.evidence: SB 10.80.22-25 'ku-cailaṁ malinaṁ kṣāmaṁ dvijaṁ... antaḥ-pura-jano dṛṣṭvā kṛṣṇenāmala-kīrtinā / kim anena kṛtaṁ puṇyam avadhūtena bhikṣuṇā / yo 'sau tri-loka-guruṇā śrī-nivāsena sambhṛtaḥ'.

statements.claim: Rukmini herself fanned the emaciated brahmana.
statements.evidence: Pack excerpt: 'The goddess Rukmini herself fans the emaciated brahmana'; emaciation also from SB 10.80.22 'kṣāmaṁ'.

statements.claim: The two friends sat and talked of their old days together at the teacher's house.
statements.evidence: SB 10.80.26 'kathayāṁ cakratur gāthāḥ pūrvā guru-kule satoḥ' (they exchanged tales of the past, having been together at the guru's house).

notes: Embrace, seating, foot-washing, incense/lamps, palace women's wonder, Rukmini fanning, and guru-kula reminiscence all supported by SB 10.80.16-26.

statements.claim: Sudama walked home from Dwaraka with empty hands — he had not been able to ask Krishna for anything.
statements.evidence: SB 10.81.13 'sa cālabdhvā dhanaṁ kṛṣṇān na tu yācitavān svayam' (he obtained wealth from Krishna but had not himself asked); corpus chain DKS_0289 (returns home empty-handed).

statements.claim: Krishna had eaten his handful of flat rice with delight.
statements.evidence: SB 10.81.34 'mayopaṇītaṁ pṛthukaika-muṣṭiṁ pratyagrahīt prīti-yuto mahātmā' (the great soul joyfully accepted the single handful of flat rice I brought); corpus chain DKS_0289.

statements.claim: Walking, Sudama reflected: 'Where am I, poor and full of faults, and where is Krishna, the very home of fortune?'
statements.evidence: SB 10.81.15 'kvāhaṁ daridraḥ pāpīyān kva kṛṣṇaḥ śrī-niketanaḥ'.

statements.claim: He understood that if he had been given wealth after asking, he might have grown proud and forgotten Krishna; the Lord had given him prosperity unasked, and does not grant the devotee the riches and glories that would pull the heart away.
statements.evidence: SB 10.81.19 'adhano 'yaṁ dhanaṁ prāpya mādyann uccair na māṁ smaret'; 10.81.36 'bhaktāya citrā bhagavān hi sampado rājyaṁ vibhūtīr na samarthayaty ajaḥ'.

statements.claim: Sudama prayed that this friendship, companionship and service be his in birth after birth.
statements.evidence: SB 10.81.35 'tasyaiva me sauhṛda-sakhya-maitrī-dāsyaṁ punar janmani janmani syāt'.

statements.claim: At the edge of his village he found his hut replaced by celestial mansions ringed with gardens and lakes loud with birds, and well-dressed men and graceful women moving through the courtyards.
statements.evidence: SB 10.81.21-22 'vicitropavanodyānaiḥ kūjad-dvija-kulākulaiḥ... juṣṭaṁ sv-alaṅkṛtaiḥ pumbhiḥ strībhiś ca hariṇākṣibhiḥ'.

statements.claim: His wife heard he had come, hurried out in great excitement, radiant as the goddess of fortune among her attendants, and her eyes filled with tears of love.
statements.evidence: SB 10.81.24-26 'patim āgatam ākarṇya patny uddharṣāti-sambhramā / pati-vratā patiṁ dṛṣṭvā premotkaṇṭhāśru-locanā / patnīṁ vīkṣya visphurantīṁ devīṁ vaimānikīm iva'.

statements.claim: Inside, the beds were soft as foam, spread with ivory and gold; golden seats, clear crystal walls with great emeralds, and abundant riches filled the house.
statements.evidence: SB 10.81.28-31 'payaḥ-phena-nibhāḥ śayyā dāntā rukma-paricchadāḥ / āsanāni ca haimāni... svaccha-sphaṭika-kuḍyeṣu mahā-mārakateṣu... samṛddhīḥ sarva-sampadām'.

statements.claim: He reflected that the Lord gives generously even to one who asks in person, and accepted even his meager single handful of flat rice with joy — Krishna had given unasked, so that the giving never came between them.
statements.evidence: SB 10.81.33-34 'nanv abruvāṇo diśate samakṣaṁ yāciṣṇave bhūry api bhūri-bhojaḥ / kiñcit karoty urv api yat sva-dattaṁ suhṛt-kṛtaṁ phalgv api bhūri-kārī mayopaṇītaṁ pṛthukaika-muṣṭiṁ pratyagrahīt prīti-yuto mahātmā'; 10.81.37 'bhakto 'tīva janārdane'.

statements.claim: Sudama reflects this happened because he asked for nothing but to remain Krishna's friend.
statements.evidence: Interpretive summary of the unasked-grace theme (10.81.13, 33-36); consistent with the pack's reading but phrased beyond the verses.

notes: Transformation of the hut into a celestial palace, wife's radiant welcome, inner riches, and Sudama's reflections all trace directly to SB 10.81.13-37.

statements.claim: The sages at Samanta-panchaka, pleased with Vasudeva's question about the highest duty, chose him and initiated him into a great sacrifice there, with Vasudeva choosing them as his priests as dharma directs.
statements.evidence: Pack index summary: 'The sages, pleased with Vasudeva's question, initiate him and he performs a great sacrifice at Samanta-panchaka'; SB 10.84.42 'ta enam ṛṣayo rājan vṛtā dharmeṇa dhārmikam'; 10.84.43 'tad-dīkṣāyāṁ pravṛttāyāṁ'.

statements.claim: The sage Narada was among the gathered rishis watching the preparations.
statements.evidence: Narada listed in the pack's canonical-event characters for evt_0494 (alongside Vasudeva, Krishna, Balarama, the sages); consistent with ch. 10.84 context.

statements.claim: The Vrishnis arrived wearing lotus garlands, and Vasudeva's queens came delighted, bright with gold necklaces and fine garments.
statements.evidence: SB 10.84.43-44 'vṛṣṇayaḥ puṣkara-srajaḥ / tan-mahiṣyaś ca muditā niṣka-kaṇṭhyaḥ su-vāsasaḥ'.

statements.claim: The field resounded with mridangas, drums, conches and kettledrums.
statements.evidence: SB 10.84.45 'nedur mṛdaṅga-paṭaha-śaṅkha-bhery-ānakādayaḥ'.

statements.claim: The priests anointed Vasudeva according to rite, his body touched with unguents, and dressed him in silks, bracelets, necklaces, anklets and earrings; his priests were robed in jeweled silk.
statements.evidence: SB 10.84.46-48 'tam abhyaṣiñcan vidhi-vad aktam abhyaktam ṛtvijaḥ / tābhir dukūla-valayair hāra-nūpura-kuṇḍalaiḥ / tasyartvijo... ratna-kauśeya-vāsasaḥ'.

statements.claim: Krishna and Balarama were present among the kinsmen, each with his own family and sons.
statements.evidence: SB 10.84.49 'tadā rāmaś ca kṛṣṇaś ca svaiḥ svair bandhubhir anvitau'; pack excerpt: 'Krishna and Balarama shine there among their kinsmen and sons'.

statements.claim: Vasudeva performed the subsidiary rites such as agnihotra as prescribed, and at the proper time gave the priests their dakshina — rich gifts of cows, land and maidens.
statements.evidence: SB 10.84.50-51 'īje 'nu-yajñaṁ vidhinā agni-hotrādi-lakṣaṇaiḥ / athartvigbhyo 'dadāt kāle yathāmnātaṁ sa dakṣiṇāḥ'; pack excerpt: 'rich gifts of cows, land and maidens to the priests'.

statements.claim: The sages completed the ritual with the queens' offerings and the avabhritha bath; after bathing, Vasudeva gave garments and ornaments to the bards and to the women.
statements.evidence: SB 10.84.52-53 'patnī-saṁyājāvabhṛthyaiś caritvā te maharṣayaḥ / snāto 'laṅkāra-vāsāṁsi vandibhyo 'dāt tathā striyaḥ'.

statements.claim: He gave abundant gifts to his kinsmen with their wives and sons, and honored the assembled priests, gods, men, ancestors and caranas.
statements.evidence: SB 10.84.54-55 'bandhūn sa-dārān sa-sutān pāribarheṇa bhūyasā / sadasyartvik-sura-gaṇān nṛ-bhūta-pitṛ-cāraṇān'.

statements.claim: Background that wise men had come to Samanta-panchaka for ages and the ground was blessed is generic holy-place coloring.
statements.evidence: Pack calls it 'that holy field'; the 'for ages' claim is atmosphere, not a pack assertion.

notes: Sacrifice sequence, attendants, gifts and avabhritha all match SB 10.84.42-55 closely.

statements.claim: Years before, after their studies, Krishna and Balarama had fetched back their teacher's dead son as his fee, urged by the guru.
statements.evidence: SB 10.85.31 'cirān mṛta-sutādāne guruṇā kila coditau' (urged by the guru to give back a son dead long ago); pack excerpt: 'they had once fetched their guru's dead son as a fee'; the brothers' journey to the world of the dead is carried by the corpus chain.

statements.claim: Devaki, remembering her sons slain by Kamsa, tearfully asked Krishna and Balarama to bring back her dead children, entreating: 'You two are the lords of the masters of yoga; you fetched a long-dead son for your teacher — grant my wish the same way.'
statements.evidence: SB 10.85.26-32: 'devakī... kṛṣṇa-rāmau samāśrāvya putrān kaṁsa-vihiṁsitān... cirān mṛta-sutādāne guruṇā kila coditau / tathā me kurutaṁ kāmaṁ yuvāṁ yogeśvareśvarau'; pack excerpt confirms tears and request.

statements.claim: Devaki had borne children whom Kamsa killed one by one at birth, because he feared a son of hers would take his kingdom and life.
statements.evidence: Corpus chain: DKS_0004-DKS_0011 — the prophecy that Devaki's eighth child would kill Kamsa, and Kamsa destroying her children as they were born ('dashing each of them the moment it came into the world', DKS_0010); pack excerpt: 'the sons slaughtered by Kamsa... slain by the Bhoja king'.

statements.claim: She called the six slain the ones 'the Bhoja king slew' — Kamsa being the Bhoja king.
statements.evidence: Pack excerpt: 'entreats them to bring back the sons slain by the Bhoja king' (i.e., Kamsa); SB 10.85.32.

statements.claim: The tale of the restored teacher's son was told everywhere and reopened Devaki's old grief, moving her to ask.
statements.evidence: Pack says only that Devaki, 'hearing of how Krishna and Balarama had brought back their guru's son... tearfully asks'; the city-wide fame and her inner turmoil are connective psychology.

statements.claim: Krishna and Balarama did not refuse her; in their silence Devaki felt heard and dared to hope.
statements.evidence: Pack verses 26-32 end at her request; no response is recorded in this excerpt, so the brothers' silence and her hope are connective closure (fulfillment follows in DKS_0293).

notes: Request itself and its framing (guru-son precedent, six sons slain by Kamsa/Bhoja king, plea to the lords of yoga) fully supported by SB 10.85.26-32; backstory grounded in corpus chain.

statements.claim: Krishna and Balarama descended by their mystic power (yoga-maya) into Sutala, the realm of the daitya king Bali.
statements.evidence: Pack excerpt: 'Entering Sutala by their yoga-maya, Krishna and Balarama are received by the daitya king Bali'; SB 10.85.34 'tasmin praviṣṭāv upalabhya daitya-rāḍ'.

statements.claim: Bali rose at once, bowed low with his whole family, his heart overflowing with joy at the sight, settled them on a noble seat, and worshipped them with garments of great worth, ornaments and unguents.
statements.evidence: SB 10.85.34-36 'sadyaḥ samutthāya nanāma sānvayaḥ / tad-darśanāhlāda-pariplutāśayaḥ... samarhayām āsa sa tau vibhūtibhir mahārha-vastrābharaṇānulepanaiḥ'.

statements.claim: Bali washed their feet with his kin and repeatedly pressed the lotus feet to his head, his mind dissolved in love.
statements.evidence: SB 10.85.37 'sa indraseno bhagavat-padāmbujaṁ bibhran muhuḥ prema-vibhinnayā dhiyā'; pack excerpt: 'washes their feet with his kin'.

statements.claim: Bali said their sight is hard to obtain — daityas, danavas, gandharvas, siddhas, vidyadharas and caranas approach with enmity or longing and none can comprehend them — and begged: 'From the dark well of this world you have drawn me up; instruct me, make me sinless.'
statements.evidence: SB 10.85.39-45: 'darśanaṁ vāṁ hi bhūtānāṁ duṣprāpaṁ... kecanodbaddha-vaireṇa bhaktyā kecana kāmataḥ... tava yogeśvareśvara / tan naḥ prasīda... andha-kūpāt niṣkramya... / śādhy asmān īśitavyeśa niṣpāpān kuru naḥ prabho'.

statements.claim: Krishna revealed that the six sons who were born in Devaki's womb and slain by Kamsa were once the six sons of the sage Marichi, who laughed at Brahma and were cursed to be born as demons; they now dwelt nearby awaiting release, and Krishna would take them back to end his mother's grief.
statements.evidence: SB 10.85.47-49 'tenāsurīm agan yonim... devakyā udare jātā rājan kaṁsa-vihiṁsitāḥ / ita etān praṇeṣyāmo mātṛ-śokāpanuttaye'; pack excerpt: 'the six sons were once the six sons of Marichi, who laughed at Brahma and were cursed to be born as demons... who now dwell nearby awaiting release'.

statements.claim: Having spoken, Krishna took the six sons into his keeping, and the brothers rose from Sutala carrying them with them, honored as they departed.
statements.evidence: SB 10.85.51 'ity uktvā tān samādāya indrasenena pūjitau' (having said this and taken them, honored by Indrasena/Bali's line).

statements.claim: The six sons of Marichi passing through many births to this waiting, and their deaths at Kamsa's hands being 'only a pause', is interpretive framing.
statements.evidence: Consistent with the curse-and-release arc (10.85.47-49) but phrased as narrative commentary beyond the pack text.

notes: Bali's reception, speech, Krishna's revelation of the Marichi origin, and the taking of the six sons all match SB 10.85.33-51.
